title: From Disengaged to Selective: The Profiles of Young Adult Daters
gist: Latent class analysis of the Wheatley Institute's 2025 National Dating Landscape Survey (N=4,539) finds three young-adult dater profiles: Unprepared/Disengaged (37%), Selective/Serious (45%) and Active/Social (18%). Low-frequency dating splits into low-resource, low-confidence people and serious daters struggling to find partners, so interventions must be tailored.

insights.claim: Less than a third of young adults aged 22-35 who expect to marry are dating at least once a month, and 29% of men and 38% of women in this age group report not dating at all in the last year.
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: Quantifies the 'dating recession', a leading indicator for later declines in marriage and births.
insights.locator: In our previous research using the Wheatley Institute’s 2025 National Dating Landscape Survey

insights.claim: The three dater types are equally dissatisfied with their dating options, their attitudes about financial milestones before marriage are not widely different, and there is no age difference among them.
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: Dissatisfaction is universal, so differences in dating frequency stem from resources, confidence and orientation, not age or finances alone.

insights.claim: Money was the most endorsed barrier to dating in the survey.
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: Cost of dating is a constraint; relevant to affordability and low-cost social venues.

insights.claim: 37% of young adults are 'Unprepared Daters', who date only once or twice a year, have the furthest marital horizon (almost 7 years), the lowest marital salience and the lowest dating confidence.
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: The largest low-engagement cohort suggests a pipeline of delayed or forgone marriage and fertility.

insights.claim: Unprepared Daters are less well-off, less likely to have advanced education, are much less likely to be working (23%) or working full time (37%), are somewhat more liberal, 47% never attend religious services, and have poorer physical and mental health.
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: Dating disengagement correlates with economic and health disadvantage, linking labor-market weakness to family-formation decline.
insights.locator: Comparatively, they are less well-off financially

insights.claim: Unprepared Daters lack resources and confidence, so parents and educators can help most by building dating skills and surfacing lower-cost dating options.
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: Points to demand for skills-based and low-cost dating programs.

insights.claim: About 45% of young adults are 'Serious/Selective Daters', who date only a few times a year but with seriousness and selectivity, have the highest dating confidence and the shortest marital horizon (still 4-5 years out).
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: The largest group is infrequent by choice, so the dating recession partly reflects unmet demand for serious partners.

insights.claim: Selective Daters are 60% women and 40% men, the most educated group, with the lowest depression, highest body image scores, and the lowest online pornography use and AI romantic companion interaction.
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: An educated female-skewed cohort struggling to find matching partners hints at a partner-matching and educational-sorting mismatch.
insights.locator: Selective or Serious daters are split: 60% women and 40% men.

insights.claim: Selective Daters need dating pathways to find partners matching their serious orientation more than dating education, though their confidence may be misplaced.
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: Opportunity space for matchmaking and community-based introductions rather than skills coaching.

insights.claim: 18% of young adults who expect to marry are 'Active Daters', dating about once a month, who score highest on a social orientation to dating and on avoiding commitment even though they have the highest marital salience.
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: This group dates for social integration while delaying commitment, a gap between stated marriage goals and behavior.

insights.claim: Active Daters are nearly 70% men, best resourced with the highest full-time employment and income, the most politically conservative, 43% regular religious attenders, and have the highest regular pornography viewing (42%) and regular AI romantic partner interaction (30%).
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: Counterintuitive link between religiosity, resources and AI-romance/pornography use among frequent male daters; AI companions are a notable adoption pocket.

insights.claim: Active Daters have the highest negative feelings from past breakups and the strongest commitment avoidance, so practitioners should build dating resilience and explore the fears driving their hesitancy.
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: Bad past breakups plausibly drive commitment avoidance; relevant to relationship-coaching offerings.
insights.locator: And finally, “Active Daters” might be dating more frequently

insights.claim: Dating initiation and marriage formation were left almost entirely to commercial algorithms and hookup culture, leaving young adults with an acute skills and confidence deficit (Andrea Gurney, quoted).
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: Critique of app-mediated dating as an opening for non-commercial or community dating models.

insights.claim: Low-frequency dating consists of low-resourced, low-confidence daters and daters seeking but struggling to find serious relationships, while the most frequent daters date socially and fear commitment.
insights.speaker: Alan J. Hawkins, Jason S. Carroll, Brian J. Willoughby and Anna Elmer
insights.so_what: The aggregate dating recession is a mix of distinct problems, so solutions and products must be segmented.
insights.quote: Low-frequency dating is composed of low-resourced daters with low confidence, and daters looking for—but struggling to find—serious relationships.
